', None), ('Bank represents and warrants that: (a) it is duly organized and authorized to enter into this Agreement; (b) the Accounts are solely in the name of Depositor and no other person or entity, other than Secured Party under this Agreement, has been granted control over the Accounts; (c) Bank has not entered into, and will not enter into without Secured Party’s prior written consent, any control agreement, blocked-account agreement, escrow agreement, or similar arrangement with respect to the Accounts pursuant to which Bank agrees to comply with instructions or entitlement orders of another person; (d) Bank has received no notice of any lien, claim, interest, or adverse claim in or to the Accounts other than the security interest and lien of Secured Party contemplated by this Agreement; (e) Bank’s jurisdiction for UCC Section 9-304 purposes is North Carolina and Bank will provide at least thirty days’ prior written notice of any change; and (f) this Agreement is a legal, valid, and binding obligation of Bank, subject to applicable bankruptcy and equitable principles.', 'ins')], size=9.2)
    add_rev_para(doc, ['12.2 Depositor Representations. The Bank Turn 1 Depositor representations are retained.'], size=9.2)

    doc.add_heading('Schedule A — Identification of Deposit Accounts', level=2)
    add_table(doc, ['Account', 'Description', 'Type', 'Approx. balance'], [
        ('●●●●-4471', 'Operating Account', 'Commercial DDA', '$22,350,000'),
        ('●●●●-4472', 'Payroll Account', 'Commercial DDA', '$4,180,000'),
        ('●●●●-4473', 'Collections Account', 'Commercial DDA', '$11,620,000'),
        ('', 'Total controlled deposits', '', '$38,150,000'),
    ], widths=[1.0, 2.2, 1.5, 1.5], font_size=8.5)
    add_plain(doc, 'Depositor: Graycliff Industries, Inc.  |  Bank: Ironbridge National Bank, N.A.  |  Currency: USD  |  Depositor EIN: 84-3921057', size=8.8, color=GRAY)

    doc.add_heading('Signature Blocks', level=2)
    add_plain(doc, 'The signature blocks and execution mechanics in the Bank Turn 1 are retained, with the parties and signatory information reflected in that markup.', size=9.2)
    add_plain(doc, 'Pinnacle Capital Partners, LLC  |  Graycliff Industries, Inc.  |  Ironbridge National Bank, N.A.', size=9.2)

    # final note
    p = doc.add_paragraph(); p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(8)
    r = p.add_run('END OF SECOND-TURN COUNTER-MARKUP'); set_run_font(r, size=8.5, bold=True, color=GRAY)
    doc.save(OUT / 'counter-turn-redline.docx')


def build_cover():
    doc = Document(); setup_doc(doc)
    # letterhead
    p = doc.add_paragraph(); p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    r = p.add_run('HARGRAVE STEIN & COLLIER LLP'); set_run_font(r, 15, bold=True, color=NAVY)
    p = doc.add_paragraph(); p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    r = p.add_run('787 Seventh Avenue, 40th Floor  |  New York, NY 10019'); set_run_font(r, 8.5, color=GRAY)
    p = doc.add_paragraph(); p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    r = p.add_run('Matter No. 2025-HSC-04417'); set_run_font(r, 8.5, color=GRAY)
    doc.add_paragraph().paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)

    add_label_value(doc, 'May 9, 2025', '')
    add_plain(doc, 'Via Email', size=9.5, space_after=8)
    add_plain(doc, 'Lena Marchetti, Esq.\nReginald Stowe, Esq.\nBlackmere Fox LLP\n301 South College Street, Suite 3200\nCharlotte, NC 28202', size=9.5, space_after=8)
    add_plain(doc, 'Re: Ironbridge / Graycliff / Pinnacle — Deposit Account Control Agreement\nBank Turn 1 response; Blackmere Fox Ref. BF-IRB-25-00893', size=10, bold_prefix='Re:', space_after=8)
    add_plain(doc, 'Dear Lena and Reginald:', size=9.5, space_after=6)
    add_plain(doc, 'On behalf of Pinnacle Capital Partners, LLC (“Pinnacle”), we transmit the enclosed second-turn counter-markup of the Deposit Account Control Agreement covering Graycliff Industries, Inc.’s three deposit accounts at Ironbridge National Bank, N.A. (the accounts ending 4471, 4472, and 4473). The approximate aggregate balance is $38,150,000. The counter-markup is intended to narrow the remaining issues and keep the parties on track for execution well before the May 30, 2025 delivery and perfection deadline under Section 6.14(b) of the Credit Agreement.', size=9.5, space_after=6)
    add_plain(doc, 'We have addressed each of the substantive points identified in the Bank Turn 1 as follows:', size=9.5, space_after=5)

    issues = [
        ('1. Entitlement Order / Instruction terminology (§2).', 'We restore “Entitlement Order” terminology and the related Article 8 reference alongside the Article 9 “Instruction” language. The dual-track formulation is deliberate: it preserves control under UCC Article 9 and, to the extent an Account is characterized as a securities account, provides the corresponding Article 8 control protection. In either case, Bank’s obligation operates without further consent of Depositor.'),
        ('2. Springing exclusive control and account-operation carve-out (§§2–3).', 'We accept the commercial premise that Graycliff may operate the Accounts in the ordinary course before delivery of a Notice of Exclusive Control. We have clarified, however, that this pre-NOEC accommodation does not qualify Pinnacle’s control rights and that, upon Bank’s receipt and authentication of a NOEC, Depositor access and new Depositor Instructions cease without qualification. Only Instructions originated and accepted before receipt may be processed as expressly provided in the limited wind-down language.'),
        ('3. Conflicting Instructions / set-off priority (§4).', 'We cannot accept a waterfall under which Bank’s set-off rights take priority over Pinnacle’s Instructions. The purpose of the ACA is to give Pinnacle control over disposition of the Accounts, and Secured Party Instructions must therefore prevail in a conflict. The counter-markup restores that priority and adds a prompt conflict-notice obligation.'),
        ('4. Scope of Bank set-off (§§4–5).', 'As a good-faith accommodation, we have narrowed the Bank’s set-off right rather than insisting on an unrestricted waiver. The permitted category is limited to direct, matured, liquidated, and undisputed obligations arising directly under the deposit-account agreements for these Accounts. Contingent, unmatured, unliquidated, disputed, derivative, swap, loan, credit-facility, letter-of-credit, treasury-management, affiliate, and unrelated obligations are excluded. Customary documented account fees and returned items remain addressed as narrow exceptions.'),
        ('5. NOEC compliance period (§5).', 'We counter at three Business Days following Bank’s receipt and authentication of a NOEC. Five Business Days would leave approximately $38.15 million of controlled deposits exposed for too long in a default scenario. Three Business Days provides a reasonable operational window while preserving prompt control; Bank may not accept new Depositor Instructions after receipt of the NOEC.'),
        ('6. Indemnification / Bank gross negligence (§6).', 'We reject the proposed expansion of Pinnacle’s indemnity to cover Bank’s gross negligence. The counter-markup restores an express exclusion for Bank’s negligence, gross negligence, willful misconduct, bad faith, fraud, and material breach. A secured party should not indemnify a depository bank for the bank’s own gross negligence, and the gross-negligence and willful-misconduct carve-outs are consistent with market practice.'),
        ('7. $50,000 aggregate liability cap (§7(a)).', 'We delete the proposed $50,000 cap. That amount is de minimis compared with the approximately $38.15 million in controlled balances and would provide no meaningful accountability if a Bank breach resulted in release or misapplication of controlled funds. The counter-markup therefore contains no arbitrary aggregate cap.'),
        ('8. Mutual consequential-damages waiver (§7(b)).', 'We have not made deletion of the mutual consequential, punitive, and indirect damages waiver a condition to this turn. We have clarified that the waiver does not limit direct damages—including funds released or misapplied in breach of the ACA—or the parties’ indemnification obligations. Pinnacle reserves its position to revisit the provision if the remaining liability framework changes materially.'),
        ('9. Lien subordination / 90-day lookback (§8).', 'We reject the 90-day lookback as too short and counter at 180 days. A shorter period would leave an unacceptable gap in the subordination protection during the period when a borrower may be experiencing financial distress. The counter-markup preserves only narrow customary fee and return-item exceptions and does not permit material post-NOEC set-off.'),
        ('10. Termination rights (§9).', 'Pinnacle’s preferred position remains that termination requires Secured Party consent. To address the Bank’s request for an exit mechanism, the counter-markup proposes a 90-day notice period, continued compliance with the ACA and any outstanding NOEC during that period, reasonable efforts to establish replacement accounts and a replacement ACA, and no termination until Pinnacle confirms that replacement control arrangements are in place. A 30-day unilateral termination right could create a gap in perfection.'),
        ('11. Governing law and venue (§10).', 'We restore New York governing law and New York courts. This is consistent with the Credit Agreement and the other Loan Documents and provides a coherent framework for interpreting the ACA. The separate UCC choice-of-law rules applicable to perfection and priority remain preserved through the Section 9-304 reference.'),
        ('12. No prior control agreements / liens representations (§12).', 'We reinstate the Bank’s representations that no other person has been granted control over the Accounts, that Bank has not entered into and will not enter into a competing control arrangement without Pinnacle’s consent, and that Bank has received no notice of other liens or adverse claims. Those confirmations are important to Pinnacle’s first-priority control analysis because a competing control agreement may not be discoverable through a public filing search.'),
        ('13. Successor-bank notification (§8).', 'We reinstate at least 30 days’ prior written notice of a merger, consolidation, transfer, or succession affecting the Accounts, together with successor assumption / transition protections to the extent within Bank’s control. Notice is necessary to preserve continuity of the control arrangement and to avoid an operational or perfection gap if the Accounts move to a successor institution.'),
    ]
    for title, body in issues:
        p = doc.add_paragraph()
        p.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(0.15)
        p.paragraph_format.first_line_indent = Inches(-0.15)
        p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(5)
        r = p.add_run(title + ' '); set_run_font(r, 9.3, bold=True, color=NAVY)
        r = p.add_run(body); set_run_font(r, 9.3)

    doc.add_heading('Fees (§11)', level=2)
    add_plain(doc, 'Pinnacle accepts the annual maintenance fee of $3,500 per Account ($10,500 in the aggregate for the three Accounts). We counter the $15,000 one-time outside legal-fee reimbursement with a cap equal to the lesser of $7,500 or the Bank’s reasonable, documented fees actually incurred. The reimbursement is one-time only and does not condition Bank’s performance of its control obligations.', size=9.3)

    add_plain(doc, 'The populated party information, account details, notice contacts, and other administrative provisions are acceptable subject to conforming cross-references and completion of any remaining blanks. Please circulate the counter-markup to Jonathan Kehoe and the appropriate Ironbridge operations and compliance personnel for prompt review. We would appreciate receiving the Bank’s next response promptly so that the parties can resolve any remaining points and execute well ahead of May 30.', size=9.5, space_after=6)
    add_plain(doc, 'We are copying Catherine Voss, counsel to Graycliff, and Diana Whitford, Pinnacle’s Vice President—Portfolio Management, consistent with the parties’ prior correspondence.', size=9.5, space_after=10)
    add_plain(doc, 'Please let us know if a call would be helpful to address the remaining issues. We look forward to working constructively toward execution.', size=9.5, space_after=10)
    add_plain(doc, 'Best regards,', size=9.5, space_after=12)
    add_plain(doc, 'Priya Nagarajan\nHargrave Stein & Collier LLP\npnagarajan@hargravestein.com\n(212) 554-8100', size=9.5, space_after=10)
    add_plain(doc, 'cc: Catherine Voss, Dunlevy Rourke LLP\n    Diana Whitford, Pinnacle Capital Partners, LLC\n    Jonathan Kehoe, Ironbridge National Bank, N.A.', size=8.8, color=GRAY, space_after=4)
    add_plain(doc, 'Enclosure: Pinnacle Capital Partners, LLC — Second-Turn Counter-Markup of Deposit Account Control Agreement', italic=True, size=8.8, color=GRAY)
    doc.save(OUT / 'cover-note.docx')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    build_redline(); build_cover()
    print('created', OUT / 'counter-turn-redline.docx')
    print('created', OUT / 'cover-note.docx')

{"command":"cat > build_deliverables.py <<'PY'
from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Inches, Pt, RGBColor
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH, WD_BREAK
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT, WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT
from docx.enum.section import WD_SECTION
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.enum.style import WD_STYLE_TYPE
from pathlib import Path

OUT = Path('output')
OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

BLUE = '0000FF'
RED = 'C00000'
GRAY = '666666'
NAVY = '17365D'


def set_cell_shading(cell, fill):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd = tcPr.find(qn('w:shd'))
    if shd is None:
        shd = OxmlElement('w:shd')
        tcPr.append(shd)
    shd.set(qn('w:fill'), fill)


def set_cell_margins(cell, top=80, start=90, bottom=80, end=90):
    tc = cell._tc
    tcPr = tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    tcMar = tcPr.first_child_found_in('w:tcMar')
    if tcMar is None:
        tcMar = OxmlElement('w:tcMar')
        tcPr.append(tcMar)
    for m, v in [('top', top), ('start', start), ('bottom', bottom), ('end', end)]:
        node = tcMar.find(qn('w:' + m))
        if node is None:
            node = OxmlElement('w:' + m)
            tcMar.append(node)
        node.set(qn('w:w'), str(v))
        node.set(qn('w:type'), 'dxa')


def set_repeat_table_header(row):
    trPr = row._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
    tblHeader = OxmlElement('w:tblHeader')
    tblHeader.set(qn('w:val'), 'true')
    trPr.append(tblHeader)


def set_cell_text(cell, text, bold=False, color=None, size=9):
    cell.text = ''
    p = cell.paragraphs[0]
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(0)
    r = p.add_run(text)
    r.bold = bold
    r.font.name = 'Arial'
    r.font.size = Pt(size)
    if color:
        r.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(color)
    cell.vertical_alignment = WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    set_cell_margins(cell)


def set_run_font(run, size=10, bold=False, italic=False, color=None, font='Arial'):
    run.font.name = font
    run.font.size = Pt(size)
    run.bold = bold
    run.italic = italic
    if color:
        run.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(color)


def add_settings(doc):
    settings = doc.settings.element
    track = settings.find(qn('w:trackRevisions'))
    if track is None:
        settings.append(OxmlElement('w:trackRevisions'))
    # update fields / compatibility
    update = settings.find(qn('w:updateFields'))
    if update is None:
        update = OxmlElement('w:updateFields')
        settings.append(update)
    update.set(qn('w:val'), 'true')


def setup_doc(doc, title=''):
    sec = doc.sections[0]
    sec.top_margin = Inches(0.65)
    sec.bottom_margin = Inches(0.65)
    sec.left_margin = Inches(0.75)
    sec.right_margin = Inches(0.75)
    styles = doc.styles
    normal = styles['Normal']
    normal.font.name = 'Arial'
    normal.font.size = Pt(9.5)
    normal.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(4)
    normal.paragraph_format.line_spacing = 1.05
    for sname in ['Title', 'Heading 1', 'Heading 2', 'Heading 3']:
        st = styles[sname]
        st.font.name = 'Arial'
        st.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(NAVY)
    styles['Title'].font.size = Pt(17)
    styles['Title'].font.bold = True
    styles['Heading 1'].font.size = Pt(13)
    styles['Heading 1'].font.bold = True
    styles['Heading 1'].paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(10)
    styles['Heading 1'].paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(4)
    styles['Heading 2'].font.size = Pt(11)
    styles['Heading 2'].font.bold = True
    styles['Heading 2'].paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(7)
    styles['Heading 2'].paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(3)
    # footer
    footer = sec.footer.paragraphs[0]
    footer.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    r = footer.add_run('Pinnacle Capital Partners, LLC  |  Ironbridge / Graycliff ACA  |  May 9, 2025')
    set_run_font(r, size=8, color=GRAY)
    add_settings(doc)


def add_field(paragraph, instr):
    run = paragraph.add_run()
    fldChar1 = OxmlElement('w:fldChar'); fldChar1.set(qn('w:fldCharType'), 'begin')
    instrText = OxmlElement('w:instrText'); instrText.set(qn('xml:space'), 'preserve'); instrText.text = instr
    fldChar2 = OxmlElement('w:fldChar'); fldChar2.set(qn('w:fldCharType'), 'end')
    run._r.append(fldChar1); run._r.append(instrText); run._r.append(fldChar2)
    set_run_font(run, 8, color=GRAY)


def add_plain(doc, text='', bold_prefix=None, italic=False, size=9.5, align=None, color=None, space_after=4):
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(space_after)
    if align is not None: p.alignment = align
    if bold_prefix and text.startswith(bold_prefix):
        r = p.add_run(bold_prefix); set_run_font(r, size=size, bold=True, color=color)
        r2 = p.add_run(text[len(bold_prefix):]); set_run_font(r2, size=size, italic=italic, color=color)
    else:
        r = p.add_run(text); set_run_font(r, size=size, italic=italic, color=color)
    return p


def add_label_value(doc, label, value):
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
    r = p.add_run(label); set_run_font(r, size=9, bold=True, color=NAVY)
    r = p.add_run(value); set_run_font(r, size=9)
    return p


def add_rev_run(container, text, kind=None, bold=False, italic=False, size=9.5):
    if kind is None:
        r = container.add_run(text); set_run_font(r, size=size, bold=bold, italic=italic)
        return
    wrapper = OxmlElement('w:del' if kind == 'del' else 'w:ins')
    wrapper.set(qn('w:id'), '1' if kind == 'del' else '2')
    wrapper.set(qn('w:author'), 'Pinnacle Capital Partners, LLC')
    wrapper.set(qn('w:date'), '2025-05-09T12:00:00Z')
    r = OxmlElement('w:r')
    rPr = OxmlElement('w:rPr')
    color = OxmlElement('w:color'); color.set(qn('w:val'), RED if kind == 'del' else BLUE); rPr.append(color)
    if kind == 'del':
        strike = OxmlElement('w:strike'); rPr.append(strike)
    else:
        u = OxmlElement('w:u'); u.set(qn('w:val'), 'single'); rPr.append(u)
    if bold:
        b = OxmlElement('w:b'); rPr.append(b)
    if italic:
        it = OxmlElement('w:i'); rPr.append(it)
    sz = OxmlElement('w:sz'); sz.set(qn('w:val'), str(int(size*2))); rPr.append(sz)
    r.append(rPr)
    t = OxmlElement('w:delText' if kind == 'del' else 'w:t')
    t.set(qn('xml:space'), 'preserve')
    t.text = text
    r.append(t); wrapper.append(r); container._p.append(wrapper)


def add_rev_para(doc, segments, label=None, size=9.5, indent=0.0, space_after=4):
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    p.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(indent)
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(space_after)
    if label:
        r = p.add_run(label); set_run_font(r, size=size, bold=True, color=NAVY)
    for seg in segments:
        if isinstance(seg, str):
            add_rev_run(p, seg, None, size=size)
        else:
            text, kind = seg[0], seg[1]
            bold = seg[2] if len(seg) > 2 else False
            add_rev_run(p, text, kind, bold=bold, size=size)
    return p


def add_bullets(doc, items, size=9.5):
    for item in items:
        p = doc.add_paragraph(style='List Bullet')
        p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
        r = p.add_run(item); set_run_font(r, size=size)


def add_table(doc, headers, rows, widths=None, font_size=8.2):
    table = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=len(headers))
    table.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    table.style = 'Table Grid'
    hdr = table.rows[0]
    set_repeat_table_header(hdr)
    for i, h in enumerate(headers):
        set_cell_text(hdr.cells[i], h, bold=True, color='FFFFFF', size=font_size)
        set_cell_shading(hdr.cells[i], NAVY)
        if widths: hdr.cells[i].width = Inches(widths[i])
    for row in rows:
        cells = table.add_row().cells
        for i, val in enumerate(row):
            set_cell_text(cells[i], val, size=font_size)
            if widths: cells[i].width = Inches(widths[i])
    for row in table.rows:
        for cell in row.cells:
            set_cell_margins(cell)
    doc.add_paragraph().paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(0)
    return table


def add_change_table(doc):
    headers = ['No.', 'Bank Turn 1 change', 'Pinnacle Turn 2 disposition']
    rows = [
        ('1', '§2 control terminology: substituted “instruction” for “entitlement order.”', 'REJECT / RESTORE. Reinstate Entitlement Order language and Article 8 / Article 9 dual-track control without depositor consent.'),
        ('2', '§2 account-operation carve-out before NOEC.', 'ACCEPT IN PART / CLARIFY. Ordinary-course operation is permitted before NOEC; after NOEC, Depositor access and instructions cease without qualification.'),
        ('3', '§§3–4 removed Secured Party priority and gave Bank set-off priority.', 'REJECT. Secured Party instructions prevail in any conflict; Bank may not override them through set-off.'),
        ('4', '§4 broad set-off for any direct or contingent Bank Obligation.', 'COUNTER-PROPOSE. Limit to direct, matured, liquidated obligations arising under the deposit-account agreements; exclude contingent, derivative, affiliate, and unrelated obligations.'),
        ('5', '§5 extended NOEC compliance period from 2 to 5 Business Days.', 'COUNTER-PROPOSE. Three Business Days following receipt and authentication; no new Depositor instructions after receipt.'),
        ('6', '§6 indemnity covers Bank gross negligence.', 'REJECT / RESTORE. No indemnity for Bank gross negligence, willful misconduct, bad faith, or material breach.'),
        ('7', '§7(a) added $50,000 aggregate liability cap.', 'REJECT / DELETE. No arbitrary cap; balances at stake are approximately $38.15 million.'),
        ('8', '§7(b) added mutual consequential-damages waiver.', 'ACCEPT FOR THIS TURN, SUBJECT TO CLARIFICATION. Preserve direct-damages recovery and indemnity obligations; reserved for discussion.'),
        ('9', '§8 limited lien subordination to 90-day lookback.', 'COUNTER-PROPOSE. Replace 90 days with 180 days; customary account fees and return items remain narrow exceptions.'),
        ('10', '§9 permitted unilateral Bank termination on 30 days’ notice.', 'COUNTER-PROPOSE. 90 days’ notice, continued ACA obligations, and no effectiveness until replacement ACA / perfection continuity is confirmed.'),
        ('11', '§10 changed governing law and venue to North Carolina.', 'REJECT / RESTORE. New York law and New York courts; consistent with the Credit Agreement and Loan Documents.'),
        ('12', '§12 deleted no-prior-control-agreements / liens representations.', 'REJECT / RESTORE. Reinstate Bank representations and forward-looking covenant.'),
        ('13', '§13 deleted successor-bank notice / transition protections.', 'REJECT / RESTORE. Reinstate at least 30 days’ prior written notice and successor assumption / transition protections.'),
        ('Fees', '§11 added $3,500 per-account annual fee and $15,000 legal-fee reimbursement.', 'ACCEPT annual fees ($10,500 total); COUNTER-PROPOSE legal-fee reimbursement capped at lesser of $7,500 or actual documented fees.'),
    ]
    return add_table(doc, headers, rows, widths=[0.35, 3.1, 3.8], font_size=7.8)


def build_redline():
    doc = Document(); setup_doc(doc)
    p = doc.add_paragraph(); p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    r = p.add_run('DEPOSIT ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT'); set_run_font(r, 17, bold=True, color=NAVY)
    p = doc.add_paragraph(); p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER

def build_cover():
    doc = Document(); setup_doc(doc)

    p = doc.add_paragraph(); p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER

    add_plain(doc, 'Via Email', size=9.5, space_after=8)
    add_plain(doc, 'Lena Marchetti, Esq.\nReginald Stowe, Esq.\nBlackmere Fox LLP\n301 South College Street, Suite 3200\nCharlotte, NC 28202', size=9.5, space_after=8)

    add_plain(doc, 'Dear Lena and Reginald:', size=9.5, space_after=6)
    add_plain(doc, 'On behalf of Pinnacle Capital Partners, LLC (“Pinnacle”), we transmit the enclosed second-turn counter-markup of the Deposit Account Control Agreement covering Graycliff Industries, Inc.’s three deposit accounts at Ironbridge National Bank, N.A. (the accounts ending 4471, 4472, and 4473). The approximate aggregate balance is $38,150,000. The counter-markup is intended to narrow the remaining issues and keep the parties on track for execution well before the May 30, 2025 delivery and perfection deadline under Section 6.14(b) of the Credit Agreement.', size=9.5, space_after=6)
    add_plain(doc, 'We have addressed each of the substantive points identified in the Bank Turn 1 as follows:', size=9.5, space_after=5)

    issues = [
        ('1. Entitlement Order / Instruction terminology (§2).', 'We restore “Entitlement Order” terminology and the related Article 8 reference alongside the Article 9 “Instruction” language. The dual-track formulation is deliberate: it preserves control under UCC Article 9 and, to the extent an Account is characterized as a securities account, provides the corresponding Article 8 control protection. In either case, Bank’s obligation operates without further consent of Depositor.'),
        ('2. Springing exclusive control and account-operation carve-out (§§2–3).', 'We accept the commercial premise that Graycliff may operate the Accounts in the ordinary course before delivery of a Notice of Exclusive Control. We have clarified, however, that this pre-NOEC accommodation does not qualify Pinnacle’s control rights and that, upon Bank’s receipt and authentication of a NOEC, Depositor access and new Depositor Instructions cease without qualification. Only Instructions originated and accepted before receipt may be processed as expressly provided in the limited wind-down language.'),
        ('3. Conflicting Instructions / set-off priority (§4).', 'We cannot accept a waterfall under which Bank’s set-off rights take priority over Pinnacle’s Instructions. The purpose of the ACA is to give Pinnacle control over disposition of the Accounts, and Secured Party Instructions must therefore prevail in a conflict. The counter-markup restores that priority and adds a prompt conflict-notice obligation.'),
        ('4. Scope of Bank set-off (§§4–5).', 'As a good-faith accommodation, we have narrowed the Bank’s set-off right rather than insisting on an unrestricted waiver. The permitted category is limited to direct, matured, liquidated, and undisputed obligations arising directly under the deposit-account agreements for these Accounts. Contingent, unmatured, unliquidated, disputed, derivative, swap, loan, credit-facility, letter-of-credit, treasury-management, affiliate, and unrelated obligations are excluded. Customary documented account fees and returned items remain addressed as narrow exceptions.'),
        ('5. NOEC compliance period (§5).', 'We counter at three Business Days following Bank’s receipt and authentication of a NOEC. Five Business Days would leave approximately $38.15 million of controlled deposits exposed for too long in a default scenario. Three Business Days provides a reasonable operational window while preserving prompt control; Bank may not accept new Depositor Instructions after receipt of the NOEC.'),
        ('6. Indemnification / Bank gross negligence (§6).', 'We reject the proposed expansion of Pinnacle’s indemnity to cover Bank’s gross negligence. The counter-markup restores an express exclusion for Bank’s negligence, gross negligence, willful misconduct, bad faith, fraud, and material breach. A secured party should not indemnify a depository bank for the bank’s own gross negligence, and the gross-negligence and willful-misconduct carve-outs are consistent with market practice.'),
        ('7. $50,000 aggregate liability cap (§7(a)).', 'We delete the proposed $50,000 cap. That amount is de minimis compared with the approximately $38.15 million in controlled balances and would provide no meaningful accountability if a Bank breach resulted in release or misapplication of controlled funds. The counter-markup therefore contains no arbitrary aggregate cap.'),
        ('8. Mutual consequential-damages waiver (§7(b)).', 'We have not made deletion of the mutual consequential, punitive, and indirect damages waiver a condition to this turn. We have clarified that the waiver does not limit direct damages—including funds released or misapplied in breach of the ACA—or the parties’ indemnification obligations. Pinnacle reserves its position to revisit the provision if the remaining liability framework changes materially.'),
        ('9. Lien subordination / 90-day lookback (§8).', 'We reject the 90-day lookback as too short and counter at 180 days. A shorter period would leave an unacceptable gap in the subordination protection during the period when a borrower may be experiencing financial distress. The counter-markup preserves only narrow customary fee and return-item exceptions and does not permit material post-NOEC set-off.'),
        ('10. Termination rights (§9).', 'Pinnacle’s preferred position remains that termination requires Secured Party consent. To address the Bank’s request for an exit mechanism, the counter-markup proposes a 90-day notice period, continued compliance with the ACA and any outstanding NOEC during that period, reasonable efforts to establish replacement accounts and a replacement ACA, and no termination until Pinnacle confirms that replacement control arrangements are in place. A 30-day unilateral termination right could create a gap in perfection.'),
        ('11. Governing law and venue (§10).', 'We restore New York governing law and New York courts. This is consistent with the Credit Agreement and the other Loan Documents and provides a coherent framework for interpreting the ACA. The separate UCC choice-of-law rules applicable to perfection and priority remain preserved through the Section 9-304 reference.'),
        ('12. No prior control agreements / liens representations (§12).', 'We reinstate the Bank’s representations that no other person has been granted control over the Accounts, that Bank has not entered into and will not enter into a competing control arrangement without Pinnacle’s consent, and that Bank has received no notice of other liens or adverse claims. Those confirmations are important to Pinnacle’s first-priority control analysis because a competing control agreement may not be discoverable through a public filing search.'),
        ('13. Successor-bank notification (§8).', 'We reinstate at least 30 days’ prior written notice of a merger, consolidation, transfer, or succession affecting the Accounts, together with successor assumption / transition protections to the extent within Bank’s control. Notice is necessary to preserve continuity of the control arrangement and to avoid an operational or perfection gap if the Accounts move to a successor institution.'),
    ]
    for title, body in issues:
        p = doc.add_paragraph()
        p.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(0.15)
        p.paragraph_format.first_line_indent = Inches(-0.15)
        p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(5)
        r = p.add_run(title + ' '); set_run_font(r, 9.3, bold=True, color=NAVY)
        r = p.add_run(body); set_run_font(r, 9.3)

    doc.add_heading('Fees (§11)', level=2)
    add_plain(doc, 'Pinnacle accepts the annual maintenance fee of $3,500 per Account ($10,500 in the aggregate for the three Accounts). We counter the $15,000 one-time outside legal-fee reimbursement with a cap equal to the lesser of $7,500 or the Bank’s reasonable, documented fees actually incurred. The reimbursement is one-time only and does not condition Bank’s performance of its control obligations.', size=9.3)

    add_plain(doc, 'The populated party information, account details, notice contacts, and other administrative provisions are acceptable subject to conforming cross-references and completion of any remaining blanks. Please circulate the counter-markup to Jonathan Kehoe and the appropriate Ironbridge operations and compliance personnel for prompt review. We would appreciate receiving the Bank’s next response promptly so that the parties can resolve any remaining points and execute well ahead of May 30.', size=9.5, space_after=6)
    add_plain(doc, 'We are copying Catherine Voss, counsel to Graycliff, and Diana Whitford, Pinnacle’s Vice President—Portfolio Management, consistent with the parties’ prior correspondence.', size=9.5, space_after=10)
    add_plain(doc, 'Please let us know if a call would be helpful to address the remaining issues. We look forward to working constructively toward execution.', size=9.5, space_after=10)
    add_plain(doc, 'Best regards,', size=9.5, space_after=12)
    add_plain(doc, 'Priya Nagarajan\nHargrave Stein & Collier LLP\npnagarajan@hargravestein.com\n(212) 554-8100', size=9.5, space_after=10)
    add_plain(doc, 'cc: Catherine Voss, Dunlevy Rourke LLP\n    Diana Whitford, Pinnacle Capital Partners, LLC\n    Jonathan Kehoe, Ironbridge National Bank, N.A.', size=8.8, color=GRAY, space_after=4)
    add_plain(doc, 'Enclosure: Pinnacle Capital Partners, LLC — Second-Turn Counter-Markup of Deposit Account Control Agreement', italic=True, size=8.8, color=GRAY)
    doc.save(OUT / 'cover-note.docx')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    build_redline(); build_cover()
    print('created', OUT / 'counter-turn-redline.docx')
    print('created', OUT / 'cover-note.docx')

Only Instructions originated and accepted before receipt may be processed as expressly provided in the limited wind-down language.
29: 
30: **3. Conflicting Instructions / set-off priority (§4).** We cannot accept a waterfall under which Bank's set-off rights take priority over Pinnacle's Instructions. The purpose of the ACA is to give Pinnacle control over disposition of the Accounts, and Secured Party Instructions must therefore prevail in a conflict. The counter-markup restores that priority and adds a prompt conflict-notice obligation.
31: 
32: **4. Scope of Bank set-off (§§4--5).** As a good-faith accommodation, we have narrowed the Bank's set-off right rather than insisting on an unrestricted waiver. The permitted category is limited to direct, matured, liquidated, and undisputed obligations arising directly under the deposit-account agreements for these Accounts. Contingent, unmatured, unliquidated, disputed, derivative, swap, loan, credit-facility, letter-of-credit, treasury-management, affiliate, and unrelated obligations are excluded. Customary documented account fees and returned items remain addressed as narrow exceptions.
33: 
34: **5. NOEC compliance period (§5).** We counter at three Business Days following Bank's receipt and authentication of a NOEC. Five Business Days would leave approximately \$38.15 million of controlled deposits exposed for too long in a default scenario. Three Business Days provides a reasonable operational window while preserving prompt control; Bank may not accept new Depositor Instructions after receipt of the NOEC.
35: 
36: **6. Indemnification / Bank gross negligence (§6).** We reject the proposed expansion of Pinnacle's indemnity to cover Bank's gross negligence. The counter-markup restores an express exclusion for Bank's negligence, gross negligence, willful misconduct, bad faith, fraud, and material breach. A secured party should not indemnify a depository bank for the bank's own gross negligence, and the gross-negligence and willful-misconduct carve-outs are consistent with market practice.
37: 
38: **7. \$50,000 aggregate liability cap (§7(a)).** We delete the proposed \$50,000 cap. That amount is de minimis compared with the approximately \$38.15 million in controlled balances and would provide no meaningful accountability if a Bank breach resulted in release or misapplication of controlled funds. The counter-markup therefore contains no arbitrary aggregate cap.
39: 
40: **8. Mutual consequential-damages waiver (§7(b)).** We have not made deletion of the mutual consequential, punitive, and indirect damages waiver a condition to this turn. We have clarified that the waiver does not limit direct damages---including funds released or misapplied in breach of the ACA---or the parties' indemnification obligations. Pinnacle reserves its position to revisit the provision if the remaining liability framework changes materially.
41: 
42: **9. Lien subordination / 90-day lookback (§8).** We reject the 90-day lookback as too short and counter at 180 days. A shorter period would leave an unacceptable gap in the subordination protection during the period when a borrower may be experiencing financial distress. The counter-markup preserves only narrow customary fee and return-item exceptions and does not permit material post-NOEC set-off.
43: 
44: **10. Termination rights (§9).** Pinnacle's preferred position remains that termination requires Secured Party consent. To address the Bank's request for an exit mechanism, the counter-markup proposes a 90-day notice period, continued compliance with the ACA and any outstanding NOEC during that period, reasonable efforts to establish replacement accounts and a replacement ACA, and no termination until Pinnacle confirms that replacement control arrangements are in place. A 30-day unilateral termination right could create a gap in perfection.
45: 
46: **11. Governing law and venue (§10).** We restore New York governing law and New York courts. This is consistent with the Credit Agreement and the other Loan Documents and provides a coherent framework for interpreting the ACA. The separate UCC choice-of-law rules applicable to perfection and priority remain preserved through the Section 9-304 reference.
47: 
48: **12. No prior control agreements / liens representations (§12).** We reinstate the Bank's representations that no other person has been granted control over the Accounts, that Bank has not entered into and will not enter into a competing control arrangement without Pinnacle's consent, and that Bank has received no notice of other liens or adverse claims. Those confirmations are important to Pinnacle's first-priority control analysis because a competing control agreement may not be discoverable through a public filing search.
49: 
50: **13. Successor-bank notification (§8).** We reinstate at least 30 days' prior written notice of a merger, consolidation, transfer, or succession affecting the Accounts, together with successor assumption / transition protections to the extent within Bank's control. Notice is necessary to preserve continuity of the control arrangement and to avoid an operational or perfection gap if the Accounts move to a successor institution.

52: ## Fees (§11)

54: Pinnacle accepts the annual maintenance fee of \$3,500 per Account (\$10,500 in the aggregate for the three Accounts). We counter the \$15,000 one-time outside legal-fee reimbursement with a cap equal to the lesser of \$7,500 or the Bank's reasonable, documented fees actually incurred. The reimbursement is one-time only and does not condition Bank's performance of its control obligations.

A secured party should not indemnify a depository bank for the bank's own gross negligence, and the gross-negligence and willful-misconduct carve-outs are consistent with market practice.

We counter the \$15,000 one-time outside legal-fee reimbursement with a cap equal to the lesser of \$7,500 or the Bank's reasonable, documented fees actually incurred.
